info.desc: Nebraska is the sixth studio album by Bruce Springsteen, released on September 30, 1982, by Columbia Records. Sparsely recorded on a 4-track cassette tape Portastudio 144, the songs on Nebraska were originally intended as demos of songs to be recorded with the E Street Band. However, Springsteen ultimately decided to release the demos himself. .

podcast.body: Bruce Springsteen recorded the entirety of this album between 1981 and 1982 using only a portable Fostex cassette unit. This minimalist approach showcased an early example of a major artist creating a full-length, impactful record outside of expensive, professional studio environments. "Bruce Springsteen recorded his entire Nebraska album throughout 1981 and 1982 on a portable Fortrack cassette unit."

podcast.body: Recorded between December 17, 1981, and January 3, 1982, in his home using an early Portastudio, this album began as a collection of demos intended for the E Street Band to learn and re-record in a professional studio. However, Springsteen found that he and the band could not replicate the original feeling and raw intimacy of these home recordings. Consequently, he made the decision to release the album exactly as it was made on cassette at home, which went on to sell almost 2 million copies and was an inspiration for other artists. "So Springsteen made the decision to release this album as he originally made it on cassette at home."

podcast.body: Released in 1982, this album followed "The River" and was recorded without the E Street Band, featuring a musically stripped-down and bleak sound. It tells introspective stories of various characters facing hard times, originating from demos that Stevie Van Zandt convinced Springsteen to release as a standalone album due to their unique quality. This flurry of songwriting also produced material for his subsequent album, "Born in the U.S.A." "It really was just supposed to be demos for the East Street band but Stevie vans and convinced him to release the songs as their own album as they were an interesting exercise to kind of."
